candidate.title: Quartz-Seq
candidate.scope: The middle, explicitly titled Quartz-Seq row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: poly(A) RNA priming, first-strand cDNA formation and primer digestion, cDNA poly(A) tailing/tagging, second-strand generation, depicted primer addition, and suppression-PCR cDNA enrichment. The neighboring separately titled MARS-Seq and Quartz-seq2 rows have no connecting branch and are not alternatives of this assigned Quartz-Seq card. Quartz-Chip shares WTA in the paper but is not a target depicted in this row. This extraction ends at amplified WTA cDNA; the paper-supported sequencing-library interface is explained without adding unshown operations. The LNA-primer annotation is retained as an explicit discrepancy with the matched primary implementation.

operations.label: Enrich with suppression PCR
operations.description: Amplifies cDNA with WTA primer regions while limiting enrichment of short primer-derived DNA. The output is amplified cDNA representing the poly(A) RNA sequences copied from the individual cell; amplification does not itself establish perfectly faithful recovery of every transcript.
operations.mechanism: In the primary implementation, complementary terminal sequences of short DNA can self-anneal into a 'pan-like' structure that prevents PCR-primer binding, suppressing their amplification. This is a sequence/length-dependent suppression mechanism, not an LNA-based target-selection mechanism.
operations.information_effect: Increases transcript-derived DNA abundance for downstream sequencing. Sequence identity and relative read representation can support gene-expression comparisons; amplification and byproduct suppression do not yield original-RNA molecule counts. The paper describes later fragmentation/adaptor ligation for Illumina sequencing, outside the drawn cDNA endpoint.
